comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Four mountains on one map. Checked 2026-10-21 against the resort's own sources: the grooming-report trail lists for Snowmass and Buttermilk (aspensnowmass.com, each trail with its rating) and the 2025-26 trail maps of all four mountains (their text layers give the spellings). Ratings follow the resort's maps and lists where they agree, or a map where it alone rates a run, also where OpenStreetMap rates a run one step harder (Grinder, Cookies, Lower Roch Run, Kandahar's start and three Highlands catwalks). Where the resort's own sources disagree on a rating, the harder of their ratings and OpenStreetMap's is kept, so such a run is never drawn easier than any of them (lead's decision 2026-10-22): OSM already holds the harder one at Snowmass's Cabin (black on the map, blue in the list) and Buttermilk's Ridge Trail (listed green and blue). Hidden: the World Cup course outline laid over Aspen Mountain's runs, a private residential chair at Highlands and two residential platters at The Pines (Snowmass), none of them on the resort's maps. Only dedicated terrain parks and pipes the resort lists as such get the park flag (lead's decision 2026-10-22): Buttermilk's Superpipe, Government, Spruce Face, Uncle Chuck's Glades and Alex's Alley, rated runs in OSM, which the resort lists under Pipes/Parks and its map draws inside its Freestyle Terrain Areas. Red's Rover, a green trail with small features, stays green. Extreme Terrain (EX on the maps, whose legends rank it above Expert Only; extreme in the resort's lists) is extreme here, as OSM has Aspen Mountain's T1-T6, Highlands' Audacious and Filip's Leap and Snowmass's Rock Band Chute (review of 2026-10-21).
